newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-BECKER BEATEN IN AUSTRALIAN OPEN FIRST ROUND.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BECKER BEATEN IN AUSTRALIAN OPEN FIRST ROUND.

text.p: Defending champion Boris Becker was knocked out of the Australian Open on Monday in a sensational first-round upset.
The German world number six, a two-time champion in Melbourne, was beaten 5-7 7-6 (7-4) 3-6 6-1 6-4 by Spanish clay court specialist Carlos Moya, world ranked 25.
It is not the first time that Becker has been an early casualty at the Australian grand slam.
After winning the tournament in 1991, he was knocked out in the third round the following year and in the first round of the 1993 and 1995 tournaments.
After a shaky start against the 20-year-old Moya, a finalist in the Sydney International at the weekend, Becker appeared to have the game in his control as he built up a two-sets-to-one lead.

But Moya -- a clay-court specialist whose previous career highlight was beating Becker at the Paris Open last October -- produced a succession of superbly-placed baseline passes to oust the 1996 champion.
